q: Which Meta campaigns are wasting money?

checks.what: tool: uses spend plus an outcome metric

answer:
Short answer: On Meta, several active campaigns spent material budgets but returned net ROAS well below 1 (order-date net ROAS), so they are losing contribution after ad spend. Biggest offenders (7–13 Oct 2026, default brand Tilting Heads):

- TH-383-SUSPENDER-29SEP — Ad spend: ₹24,101 · Net ROAS: 0.6x · Orders: 10 · Cost/order: ₹2,410 (low ROAS + high spend → clear loss).
- TH-383-SUSPENDER-26SEP-ADV+ — Ad spend: ₹23,526 · Net ROAS: 0.5x · Orders: 8 · Cost/order: ₹2,941.
- TH-222-WINGBIRD-23SEP — Ad spend: ₹21,626 · Net ROAS: 0.7x · Orders: 21 · Cost/order: ₹1,030.
- TH-149-SCRATCHLOUNGE-6OCT — Ad spend: ₹19,817 · Net ROAS: 0.9x · Orders: 14 · Cost/order: ₹1,415 (near breakeven but under 1).
- TH-336-PAWTECH-26SEP — Ad spend: ₹19,190 · Net ROAS: 0.9x · Orders: 12 · Cost/order: ₹1,599.
- TH-012-SNUGBOO-23SEP — Ad spend: ₹19,174 · Net ROAS: 0.7x · Orders: 15 · Cost/order: ₹1,278.
- DOG DAD T-SHIRT-CS-06OCT — Ad spend: ₹12,323 · Net ROAS: 0.5x · Orders: 8 · Cost/order: ₹1,540.

Why it matters: net ROAS <1 means the contribution margin after product costs is not covering ad spend; these campaigns are reducing net profit. Figures: ad spend (report_date) vs net ROAS / orders (order_date P&L basis). Currency: INR.

Worth checking: pause/scale-down the high-spend, low-ROAS campaigns above and drill into their top adsets/creatives to see if a small subset is responsible.

Period: 2026-10-07..2026-10-13 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-14
